answer: The network treats each answer as collateral: incoherent text on the violet scores zero and the identity stops earning. Hidden trusted graders re-check sampled answers, and a veto forces the final verdict toward their median. An attacker cannot see which lane samples which answer, so the reef of buying votes must cover the whole panel rather than one seat. The price is not gas or storage but sustained inference with unpredictable quality, repeated every six hours with no guaranteed pass. That makes the karst expensive rather than free. Seal sqttx.
